proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true admissions lag is closer to 2 weeks, forecasts may be phase-shifted early (peaks predicted too soon) and under/over-shoot around turning points.
proposals.rationale: Keeps SEIRS core (waning immunity/reinfection) while aligning hospitalization-rate observations to infections via a short 1-week reporting/admission lag; parsimonious and consistent with prior sensitivity around 1–2 weeks.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the effective lag varies over time or is shorter (≈1 week), the model can produce delayed peaks and sluggish rise/decline, degrading short-horizon accuracy.
proposals.rationale: Matches the previous best spec and directly targets the key timing misalignment by using a 2-week lag from I proxy to observed hospitalizations; retains simple non-fractional dynamics for stability.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May be over-flexible across splits, yielding higher variability/instability and occasional unrealistic curvature (over-sharpened or flattened peaks) despite good average fit.
proposals.rationale: Adds fractional flexibility to capture moderate peakiness at high rate scale while keeping the observation mapping simple (single 1-week delay) to limit instability; useful if non-fractional SEIRS underfits peak shape.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Risk of split-to-split instability/overfitting (especially with short series) and potential identifiability tradeoffs between fractional effects and lag, causing inconsistent peak timing/amplitude.
proposals.rationale: Combines the empirically strong 2-week lag with fractional dynamics to accommodate subtle non-exponential dwell-time effects without adding compartments; a targeted extension when timing is right but shape is off.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is 1–2 weeks, this will systematically lag the observed series (late peaks, late declines) and can inflate errors near rapid transitions.
proposals.rationale: Boundary sensitivity check for longer infection-to-admission delays while keeping the same SEIRS backbone; helps diagnose whether residual errors are primarily timing-related beyond 2 weeks.
